title: Principal-open affine tests suffice for universal openness
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and set $f=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi):\operatorname{Spec}(C)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every commutative $A$-algebra $B$, put $D_B=B\otimes_A C$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(b\otimes c)(b'\otimes c')=bb'\otimes cc'$ and unit $1\otimes1$, and put $q_B=\operatorname{Spec}(j_B)$ for $j_B:B\to D_B$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Write $D_{D_B}(g)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(D_B):g\notin\mathfrak p\}$. Assume that $q_B(D_{D_B}(g))$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ for every such $B$ and every $g\in D_B$. Then every $q_B$ is open, and $f$ is universally open: for every scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] and morphism $a:T\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, the projection $q:P=\operatorname{Spec}(C)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}T\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is open. More precisely, for any affine open subscheme $W\subseteq T$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and any isomorphism $W\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B)$, give $B$ the $A$-algebra structure corresponding to $a|_W$. There is an isomorphism over $W$ from $P\times_T W$ to $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A C)$, under which its map to $P$ identifies it with the open subscheme $q^{-1}(W)$ and its projection to $W$ becomes $q_B$. For every open subset $O\subseteq P$ one has
$$q(O)\cap W=q_B\bigl(O\cap q^{-1}(W)\bigr),$$
where the right side uses these identifications; this set is open in $W$ and in $T$. There is no quasi-compactness, separation, Noetherian, finite-type or nonempty-scheme hypothesis.

proof.text:
Fix an $A$-algebra $B$ and an open $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(D_B)$. By clause (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], $V=\bigcup_{D_{D_B}(g)\subseteq V}D_{D_B}(g)$. Direct images commute with arbitrary unions, so
$$q_B(V)=\bigcup_{D_{D_B}(g)\subseteq V}q_B(D_{D_B}(g)).$$
Every term is open by the hypothesis for this same $B$ and $g$, hence the union is open. Thus every $q_B$ is open, including when $D_B$ is the zero ring or $V$ is empty.

proof.text: Fix $a:T\to S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, put $X=\operatorname{Spec}(C)$ and $P=X\times_ST$, and let $W\subseteq T$ be any affine open. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] with the full opens $S\subseteq S$, $X\subseteq X$, and $W\subseteq T$. It identifies $Q=X\times_SW$ with the open subscheme $q^{-1}(W)$ of $P$, compatibly with both projections. Also $P\times_TW\cong Q$: by [def-pc-fibre-product], a map into either side is exactly a pair of maps to $X$ and $W$ with equal composites to $S$ (the map to $T$ must be the map to $W$ followed by its inclusion). These two universal descriptions give inverse morphisms, since their composites fix both projections. This identifies the specified map $P\times_TW\to P$ with that open-subscheme inclusion.

proof.text: Choose the specified isomorphism $e:W\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B)$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the morphism $a|_W$ in these coordinates is the spectrum of a unique ring map $A\to B$; use this map as the $A$-algebra structure. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $Q=X\times_SW$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B)\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(C)$: interchange the maps to the two factors, replacing the map to $W$ by its composite with $e$, and interchange back using $e^{-1}$. The composites fix the projections, so are identities. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with base ring $A$ and factor algebras $B,C$. It gives an isomorphism $Q\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A C)$ whose projection to $W$, in the coordinates $e$, is $\operatorname{Spec}(b\mapsto b\otimes1)=q_B$. Combined with step 2, this proves all the asserted scheme and projection identifications for this arbitrary choice of $W,e$.

proof.text:
Let $O\subseteq P$ be open. For $w\in W$, membership in $q(O)\cap W$ means exactly that there is $x\in O$ with $q(x)=w$; such $x$ lies in $q^{-1}(W)$. Thus
$$q(O)\cap W=q_B\bigl(O\cap q^{-1}(W)\bigr)$$
under steps 2--3. The intersection on the right is open in the open subscheme $q^{-1}(W)$, hence its image is open in $W$ by step 1 and the isomorphisms. Since $W$ is open in $T$, that image is open in $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], the affine opens $W$ cover $T$, so $q(O)=\bigcup_W(q(O)\cap W)$ is open in $T$. This includes empty $T$ and arbitrary infinite affine covers: only unions are used. Since $T,a,O$ were arbitrary, every base-changed projection is open, which is precisely the stated universal openness of $f$.
